intro: Black Pearl Emerald is a Pokémon Emerald ROM hack built on pokeemerald-expansion. These are the main features of this version.

items.title: Standard or Nuzlocke mode
items.body: Professor Birch asks which mode you want right after you choose your character. Nuzlocke mode enforces the rules for you: only the first Pokémon you meet in each area can be caught (species you already own and shinies don't use up the area), Poké Balls always catch, fainted Pokémon can't be healed or used, and losing a battle ends the challenge. Nuzlocke mode also switches Effort Values off on both sides: your Pokémon gain none and vitamins and wings have no effect, and enemy trainers battle with none either, so stats come from base stats, IVs, nature and level alone. Standard mode uses Effort Values normally.

items.title: Built-in randomizer
items.body: After the mode question, Birch offers to randomize your adventure. Pick the Randomlocke, Full or Chaos preset or set each option yourself: starters, wild Pokémon, gifts and trades, static encounters, legendaries, regular and boss trainers, abilities, level-up moves, TMs, field items, and for Chaos even types, evolutions, base stats and the type chart. Generations and Monotype limit which Pokémon appear. The default whole-game swap trades each species for exactly one other, so every Pokémon is still catchable somewhere. Your seed code, shown on your Trainer Card, lets friends play exactly the same game. The choice can't be changed later, and this site's route and trainer pages always show the normal game.

items.title: Randomizer presets
items.body: What each preset randomizes. Randomlocke suits a randomized Nuzlocke: the Pokémon you meet are random, but Gym Leaders and other bosses keep their teams. Full also randomizes bosses, abilities, moves, TMs and items. Chaos randomizes everything, including types and the type chart. Changing any option makes the preset Custom.

items.title: Badge level caps
items.body: Nuzlocke mode caps levels by progress: 15 before the first badge, rising by 9 with each badge to 78 before the eighth, 90 until you become Champion, then 100. Pokémon at the cap gain no EXP, and Rare Candies and the Day Care respect it. Standard mode has no level cap unless you switch one on with the Level Limiter, and its trainers rise gradually towards each Gym Leader instead of sitting at the cap, so the climb is smoother. In both modes, traded Pokémon obey you up to the badge cap, so one you train alongside your team never disobeys.

items.title: Starter kit and Candy Jar
items.body: You have the Running Shoes from your first step, and you can run indoors. Mom gives you the Candy Jar, Taxi Ticket, Pokévial, Pokémon Box Link, Exp. Share, Old Rod, Escape Rope and Pocket Watch, plus the Level Limiter in Standard mode. The Candy Jar never runs out and raises a Pokémon straight to the level your badges allow, in both modes.

items.title: Taxi Ticket
items.body: Opens the Fly map wherever flying is allowed, without a badge or a Pokémon that knows Fly.

items.title: DexNav
items.body: In Standard mode the DexNav comes with the Pokédex. Open it from the Start menu to see the Pokémon that live in the area, then press A to search for one, or R to register it so R starts a search in the field. Hold A to creep towards the rustling spot: running, cycling or taking too long scares the Pokémon off. Every DexNav Pokémon you defeat or catch in a row adds to your chain, which raises its level and the odds of an Egg Move, its Hidden Ability (once you have caught one), a held item, perfect IVs and a shiny. Any other battle, fleeing or leaving the area resets the chain. With the Level Limiter on, DexNav Pokémon never pass your level cap. Nuzlocke games have no DexNav, and it doesn't work in the Safari Zone or the Battle Frontier's Pike and Pyramid.

items.title: HMs work from the Bag
items.body: Every HM works while it is in your Bag: a Pokémon doesn't need to know the move, only be able to learn it. The party menu lists an HM for each Pokémon that could learn it wherever it can be used there, such as Cut in front of a tree or Surf facing water, so a Charizard can Fly but not Surf. Badge requirements still apply. With HM05 in your Bag and a Pokémon that could learn Flash in your party, dark caves are lit automatically.

items.title: Register up to five key items
items.body: Choose Register on up to five key items in the Bag. With one registered, SELECT uses it straight away. With more, SELECT opens a list of them in the field: pick one with A, or close it with B or SELECT.

items.title: Follower Pokémon and day/night
items.body: Your lead Pokémon follows you in the overworld, and the overworld is tinted by the time of day.

items.title: Battle Style
items.body: New games use the Set battle style. In Standard mode you can switch it in Options; Nuzlocke mode keeps it on Set.

items.title: Catch them all
items.body: Every Pokémon and every form that can be kept in the PC is obtainable, so a living Pokédex of all forms can be completed. Wild Pokémon with several looks, such as Vivillon, Flabébé, Deerling, Minior, Furfrou and costumed Pikachu, appear in any of them and favour forms you don't have yet. Sweets and Nectars are sold in Verdanturf's Bean Shop, and a Peat Block evolves Ursaring into Ursaluna at night or Bloodmoon Ursaluna at other times.

items.title: 41 PC boxes
items.body: The PC has 41 boxes instead of Emerald's 14: 1,230 places to keep Pokémon rather than 420, which is room for a full living Pokédex. The save format was rebuilt to hold them while keeping the protection against save corruption. Each box is copied to a backup sector before it is rewritten and your progress is committed in a single step, so a power cut or a crash while saving leaves your last completed save intact.

items.title: Bean Shop
items.body: Verdanturf's Poké Mart sells Rare Candies, every evolution stone and many evolution items. Its stock grows after the third and fourth badges, adding trade-evolution items and type-resist Berries.

items.title: Egg Move Tutor
items.body: The Egg Move Tutor in Wanda's house in Verdanturf teaches any Egg Move from a Pokémon's evolution family for one Pearl, without breeding.

items.title: Shiny odds of 1 in 512
items.body: Shiny Pokémon appear at 1 in 512 instead of 1 in 8,192.

items.title: Event islands
items.body: Juan gives you the Eon Ticket (Southern Island) and the Old Sea Map (Faraway Island). After the Hall of Fame, Dad gives you the Mystic Ticket (Navel Rock) and the Aurora Ticket (Birth Island). The Lilycove ferry sails there once you have eight badges.

items.title: Legendary Lottery Island
items.body: After you become Champion, Mirage Island off Route 130 hosts one random legendary you haven't caught yet, at level 70. Every legendary that has a home somewhere else is left out, so the island only ever offers something new — including the forms you cannot reach any other way, such as Galarian Articuno, Black and White Kyurem, Ice Rider Calyrex and Dada Zarude. An alternate form shares its ordinary form's name, so the island tells you which one it is before the battle starts. Catch one and it leaves the pool. The island also holds the Gracidea, Reveal Glass, DNA Splicers and the other form-changing key items, and after you become Champion the Bean Shop sells the Plates, Memories, Drives, Masks, Origin items and the Rusted Sword and Shield.

items.title: The Mirage Altar
items.body: A few Pokémon are made by evolving a second copy of a legendary you already have: Cosmoem, Naganadel, both Urshifu and Silvally. The stone altar at the top of Mirage Island calls back a Cosmog, Poipole, Kubfu or Type: Null you have already caught so you can battle and catch another one at level 70. It only lists the ones you have registered, so it doubles as a reminder of what is still ahead of you.

items.title: Modern mechanics
items.body: Battles use Generation 9 rules, including the physical/special split and updated moves, type matchups and EXP.

items.title: Mega Evolution
items.body: Flannery gives you the Mega Ring at the Lavaridge Gym. Over 90 Mega Stones, including Legends: Z-A stones, are placed around Hoenn. Z-Moves, Dynamax and Terastallization are not available.

items.title: Reworked Trick House
items.body: The Trick House's eight puzzles hold 32 cameo battles themed on other regions, from Kanto to Paldea, with Mega Stones and held items as rewards.

items.title: Postgame challengers
items.body: Two optional trainers wait in Ever Grande City after you become Champion. Beating them unlocks unlimited Ability Capsule and Ability Patch shops.

legendaries.intro: Levels and locations are read from this version's game data.
rules: Before you become Champion you can catch only one of the pre-Elite Four legendaries. Once you catch one, the others disappear until you become Champion.
Knocking out a legendary or running away doesn't use up your pick. It disappears until you leave the area and returns when you come back.
After you become Champion, every legendary you haven't caught returns and stays until you catch it.

The story legendaries are never lost either: Rayquaza on the Sky Pillar, Kyogre and Groudon in the cave the Weather Institute locates, and Lugia, Ho-Oh and Deoxys on the ticket islands all come back until you have actually caught them. None of them uses up your one pre-Elite Four pick.
